title: Accenture MS Office Mock Test: Common Applications & Shortcuts
description: 30 MCQs modelled on the reported Accenture 'Common Applications & MS Office' section: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Access basics, shortcut keys, browser tips and Command Prompt. Marking: +1 for each correct answer, no negative marking. Duration: 30 minutes.

questions.question: A student wants the document to be saved automatically at regular intervals so that work is not lost if the program crashes. Which feature provides this?
questions.explanation: AutoSave (cloud files) and AutoRecover (local recovery files) save work automatically at set intervals. The other features do not protect against crashes.

questions.question: Which Word feature converts selected text between UPPERCASE, lowercase, Sentence case and Title Case?
questions.explanation: Change Case (Home tab, or Shift+F3) switches the capitalization of selected text.

questions.question:
Consider these statements about proofing marks in MS Word:
I. A contextual error is underlined with a green line.
II. A spelling error is underlined with a blue line.
III. A grammatical error is underlined with a red line.

Which is correct?
options: None of the statements is correct
questions.explanation: Spelling errors get a red wavy underline, grammar errors get a blue wavy underline (green in older versions), and contextual (confused-word) errors get a blue underline. All three statements mix up the colors.

questions.question: Which key must be held down to select several separate (non-adjacent) words or phrases in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Holding Ctrl while selecting adds separate selections. Shift extends one continuous selection.

questions.question: A student wants to apply the formatting of one heading to several headings scattered across a long document using Format Painter. What should the student do?
options: Single-click Format Painter once and apply to all headings
Double-click Format Painter so it stays active, then click each heading
questions.explanation: Double-clicking Format Painter keeps it active for multiple applications (press Esc to stop). A single click applies it only once.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut centers the selected text in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+E centers text. Ctrl+C is Copy, Ctrl+J justifies, and Ctrl+R right-aligns.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut applies subscript formatting to the selected text in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+= applies subscript and Ctrl+Shift+= applies superscript. Ctrl+B is bold and Ctrl+U is underline.

questions.question: Which tab in MS Word contains the option to insert a table?
questions.explanation: Tables, pictures, shapes, headers and footers are inserted from the Insert tab.

questions.question: Which MS Word feature helps find synonyms for a selected word?
questions.explanation: The Thesaurus (Review tab, Shift+F7) suggests synonyms.

questions.question: What is the result of =AVERAGE(5,10,15) in Excel?
questions.explanation: The sum is 30 and there are 3 values, so the average is 30 / 3 = 10.

questions.question: What is the result of =CONCATENATE("Good"," ","Morning") in Excel?
questions.explanation: CONCATENATE joins the three text pieces in order, including the space in the middle.

questions.question: In Excel, the notation B8:B10 indicates:
options: A range of cells from B8 to B10, including B9
The division of B8 by B10
The sum of B8 and B10
questions.explanation: The colon defines a range, so B8:B10 covers B8, B9 and B10.

questions.question: Cells A1, A2 and A3 contain 10, 20 and 30. What does =SUM(A1:A3)/COUNT(A1:A3) return?
questions.explanation: SUM = 60 and COUNT = 3, so 60 / 3 = 20.

questions.question: A teacher uses =IF(B2>=40,"Pass","Fail") and B2 contains 35. What is displayed?
questions.explanation: 35 >= 40 is false, so IF returns the value_if_false argument, which is Fail.

questions.question: Range A1:A5 contains: 10, "Hello", an empty cell, 25, "World". What does =COUNT(A1:A5) return?
questions.explanation: COUNT counts only numeric cells (10 and 25). COUNTA would return 4 because it counts all non-empty cells.

questions.question: A manager wants to quickly summarize a large sales table by region and month by dragging fields. Which Excel feature is best?
questions.explanation: PivotTables summarize and group large datasets interactively using Rows, Columns, Values and Filters.

questions.question: What does =LEFT("ACCENTURE",3)&RIGHT("ACCENTURE",2) return?
questions.explanation: LEFT gives "ACC", RIGHT gives "RE", and the & operator joins them without a space, so the result is ACCRE.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut starts a PowerPoint presentation from the first slide?
questions.explanation: F5 starts the show from the beginning. Shift+F5 starts from the current slide.

questions.question: A student wants to design a process flow and hierarchy diagram quickly in PowerPoint. Which feature should be used?
questions.explanation: SmartArt (Insert tab) creates visual diagrams such as processes, cycles and hierarchies.

questions.question: Which PowerPoint tab is used to set the effect that plays when moving from one slide to the next?
questions.explanation: Transitions apply to slide changes. The Animations tab applies to objects within a slide.

questions.question: A presenter wants to see notes and a preview of the next slide on the laptop while the audience sees only the slides on the projector. Which feature is needed?
questions.explanation: Presenter View (Alt+F5) shows notes, timer and next-slide preview only to the presenter.

questions.question: Which PowerPoint view is best for rearranging the order of slides?
questions.explanation: Slide Sorter displays thumbnails of all slides, so you can drag them into a new order.

questions.question: An employee going on leave wants everyone who emails them to automatically receive a reply. Which Outlook feature should be set up?
questions.explanation: Automatic Replies (Out of Office Assistant) sends a preset message to people who email while you are away.

questions.question: A manager sends an announcement to 200 customers and does not want the recipients to see each other's email addresses. Which field should the addresses go in?
questions.explanation: Addresses in Bcc (blind carbon copy) are hidden from other recipients. To and Cc are visible to everyone.

questions.question: In MS Access, which object is used to retrieve only specific data, such as all customers from Pune?
questions.explanation: A query retrieves and filters data from tables using criteria. Reports present data, forms enter data, and macros automate actions.

questions.question: Which of these applications was NOT part of the first version of Microsoft Office?
questions.explanation: The first Office suite contained Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Outlook was added in later versions.

questions.question: A user wants to see the computer's IP address from the Command Prompt. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: ipconfig displays IP configuration. dir lists files, cls clears the screen, and tasklist shows running processes.

questions.question: In the Windows Command Prompt, which commands list the files in the current folder and clear the screen?
questions.explanation: dir and cls are the Windows commands. ls and clear are the Linux/macOS equivalents.

questions.question: A user accidentally closed an important browser tab. Which shortcut reopens the last closed tab?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Shift+T restores the most recently closed tab. Ctrl+T opens a new tab, Ctrl+W closes one, and Ctrl+Shift+N opens an incognito window.

questions.question: A user wants to delete a file permanently without sending it to the Recycle Bin. Which shortcut should be used?
questions.explanation: Shift+Delete deletes permanently (after confirmation). Delete alone moves the file to the Recycle Bin.
